newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai grain, oilseed market quiet on high prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai grain, oilseed market quiet on high prices.

text.p: The Thai grain and oilseed c&f market was quiet over the past week as buyers were discouraged by high Chicago prices, trade sources said on Tuesday.
The only order heard was from a medium-sized feedmill which bought 1,263 tonnes of Argentine soymeal for July shipment for $318 per tonne c&f Bangkok, they said.
"Otherwise, there was not much going on. The prices were so high and most people seemed to be well-covered for near term," said a trader from a major US trading house.

Low-protein South American soymeal was indicated around $320 per tonne c&f Bangkok while the high-protein soymeal of the same origin was quoted around $355. Local soymeal was quoted at 10.00-10.20 baht ($0.38-0.39) a kg.
There was no fresh buying of corn in the c&f market. The local feed industry is currently pushing the government to allow a 200,000-tonne zero-tariff import.
The government still maintains there is enough supply to cover industry needs until the fresh crop becomes available in July although the industry insists imports are necessary.
Local corn prices edged up this week to 4.70-4.90 baht a kg as those who thought tariff-free imports will not be allowed bought actively to cover demand.

Last month, poultry exporters bought up to 38,000 tonnes of Argentine corn. This corn is likely to face 20 percent tariff when it arrives in May or June. However, the government allowed poultry exporters a tariff refund.
The market is upbeat about news that the government cut the soymeal tariff to five percent from 10 percent at present, saying the reduction will boost soymeal imports.
The commerce ministry projected soymeal imports this year will top 800,000 tonnes while the feed industry said it will need to import as much as one million tonnes.
"With the (tariff) cut, feedmills are likely to import more soymeal as they reduced cheaper substitutes such as groundnut meal and fishmeal," said another Bangkok-based trader.
